Deepen the notch vertically to improve the legibility of the carve without breaking the dominant curved mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Widen the west-side notch slightly so the access edge reads as a clearer public threshold rather than a small indentation.
Increase the vertical reach of the notch to make the entry seam and undercut more legible at street level.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one dominant curved bar, so gesture clarity and hierarchy are strong. The bent mass resonates with the curved/terraced references and avoids a generic box. However, the public void is only lightly implied: the west-side notch is legible but shallow, and the road-edge response is not yet emphatic enough for the neighborhood-living brief. Sectionally, the form is calm and plausible for a compact mixed-use building, but it still feels more like a sculpted bar than a fully articulated active-ground street building. Overall it passes as an early massing diagram, with the main remaining weakness being the public threshold/void articulation at the access edge.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Curved pavilion mass with a central void and bridging threshold can support a neighborhood public program.
Courtyard-plaza composition and stepped low-rise hierarchy reinforce a community-oriented massing.
A rectilinear block with a carved central opening and overhang can create active ground publicness.
Elongated low-rise massing with a void and a lightweight upper canopy suggests a usable mixed ground condition.
Terraced, connected wings around a shared open space can produce a strong neighborhood/public sequence.

warnings: Parcel boundary was not provided, so containment/orientation is evaluated only from the visible massing and access edge.
No hard program-section invariant is required here, so the roof can remain simple; the main critique is ground publicness rather than section typology.
